newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabian stocks soar 22 percent in H1 1997.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabian stocks soar 22 percent in H1 1997.

text.p: Saudi stock market capitalisation soared to over 181 billion riyals ($48 billion) at the end of June 1997, up 22 percent from 148 billion riyals a year earlier, the Saudi Arabian Monetary Agency (SAMA) said on Wednesday.
SAMA's Saudi equity market statistics for the first half of 1997 showed the market also saw buoyant trade in terms of value traded, volume, daily averages and the all-share index.

The volume of trade stood at 126.3 million shares worth 21.3 billion riyals in the first six months of 1997, compared to 53.3 million shares worth 9.2 billion riyals in the same period a year earlier.
The number of transactions jumped 62 percent to 197,318 from 121,541 in the year-ago period.
SAMA said the average daily value traded in the first half of this year was 150.9 million riyals, up 132 percent from 65 million in the first six months of 1996.
The average daily turnover of shares reached 895,983 compared to 375,356 from January to June 1996.
The all-share index ended the first half of this year at 161.14 points from 130.63 a year earlier. The index closed 1996 at 153.1 points, indicating a more than five percent rise so far this year.

Banks were the biggest sector on the market, capitalised at 71.7 billion riyals at half year 1997. Industrials came second at 55.8 billion riyals, followed by electricity stocks at 20.6 billion riyals.

Services stocks were the most heavily traded in the period, accounting for 45 percent of turnover with 56.2 million shares changing hands. Banking stocks limped behind in second place with 17 percent, followed by industrials with 15 percent.

Riyad Bank continued to dominate dealings in terms of volume, value and number of transactions, the SAMA figures showed. Some 11.5 million Riyad Bank shares worth 2.97 billion riyals were bought and sold in 17,056 transactions.
Arriyadh Development was the second most heavily traded stock with 11.3 million shares, followed by Saudi Cement with 9.3 million shares.

Al Rajhi Banking and Investment Corp was the second busiest stock in value terms, with shares worth 1.98 billion riyals traded. The Saudi Basic Industries Corp came third, with shares valued at 1.76 billion riyals changing hands.
